Definition: a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):--obtain, possess, provide, purchase.
BiblicalUsage: To obtain or acquire is the word for getting hold of something, and it covers fields, wives, and truth itself. In Acts 1:18 Judas "purchased a field with the reward of iniquity," in 1 Thessalonians 4:4 a man is to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour, in Acts 8:20 Simon thinks the gift of God "may be purchased with money," and in Luke 18:12 the Pharisee boasts of tithes "of all that I possess."
TheologicalSignificance: To my mind, this word draws the line between buying and receiving: Judas bought a field and lost everything, Simon tried to buy the Spirit and was rebuked, and the things that matter are possessed, not purchased. I hold what I have as a steward, not an owner.
